episodes.title: American Engineer (Part I)
episodes.description: A 1956s promotional and recruiting film about American engineering. It opens with radio-telescope "sounds of the sun and the stars" and issues a repeated "Help wanted" call for imaginative, curious, courageous men and women to take on the challenges of the age. The film runs through the usual qualifications, such as a mathematical mind, a degree, a knack for tinkering and a state license, but argues that the one essential trait is the courage to accept constant challenge: "Challenge makes an engineer." From there it surveys engineering triumphs, including harnessing rushing water for hydroelectric power, turning rivers into routes for commerce, mass-producing goods at prices ordinary people can afford, and "blueprinting" the skylines of American cities, which it credits with the highest standard of living in history. It then tours the disciplines: petroleum engineers searching for "black gold" with seismographs and offshore rigs, mining engineers extracting everything from coal to uranium, chemical engineers acting as "catalytic agents" that turn raw materials into conveniences, and research engineers exploring the laws of the universe. It closes on the optimistic note that every discovery advances humanity's destiny "toward perfection." The tone throughout is classic postwar Cold War boosterism.
episodes.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization

episodes.title: A Report To Home Builders
episodes.description: A presentation of Stran-Steel Division, Great Lakes Steel Corporation. The film presents a report on advancements in modern construction materials and engineering developments that emerged in the 1930s, particularly focusing on strand steel as a revolutionary building material. It highlights the shift toward modern home construction in post-war America, emphasizing the importance of standardization and mass production to reduce costs and improve quality. The narrative includes practical examples of using strand steel in building multiple housing projects, showcasing its advantages such as fire resistance, ease of assembly, and labor efficiency. The film concludes with a vision for a future where durable, attractive homes are built using innovative materials, catering to the needs of American families.Keywordsmodern construction, strand steel, engineering developments, 1930s, post-war homes, standardization, mass production, fire resistance, housing projects, durable homes

episodes.title: American Maker
episodes.description: Relates how Americans build, from youth throughout life, by using their ingenuity not only in technological advancement but in everyday efforts by everyone. (From contemporary synopsis). One of a series of six films (one unfinished) produced by Detroit's Jam Handy Organization for Chevrolet, AMERICAN MAKER was shown in theaters, on television and to community groups, schools and organizations to whom it was loaned for free. Though it is a prominent example of "institutional advertising," promoting a corporation in general rather than its specific products, it specifically shows Chevrolet automobiles being manufactured and on the road. The film pays tribute to American craftspeople and industrial workers, but could also easily be read as a tribute to mass production and its designers. Full of scenes showing idealized white workers and suburban families enjoying the benefits of American mass production, the film is a noteworthy document of post-World War II and pre-Vietnam War corporate optimism. Jam Handy Production Number M-4441, completed 1960-03-04. See Maria Popova, The Marginalian, 2011-02-07, online at https://www.themarginalian.org/2011/02/07/american-maker/. Accessed 2023-06-06.
episodes.creator: Jam Handy Organization
